text:
Gabriel Vilardi is the kind of forward who lives at the net: last season Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 99th percentile among forwards for scoring chances from the home-plate area, and Evolving-Hockey rated him worth 2.4 wins, 34th among 401 forwards. This season the chances kept coming and the goals mostly didn't. He has 3 goals on 7.44 expected, shooting 6.5% against a league norm of 13.3%, and his teammates have also scored 4.83 fewer than expected with him on.

The last week looks like the turn. After one goal in his first 19 games, he scored against Dallas and Chicago, with three points in the 8-3 win in Dallas and seven shots in Chicago. Winnipeg has won six straight, and his minutes are up to 19.3 a night over his last ten.

Half of his 14 points have come on the power play, and he is never going to win a race (his top speed sits in the 4th percentile by NHL EDGE), which has never been his game. Watch the shooting percentage drift back toward normal; the chances say it should.
headline: Gabriel Vilardi's goals are coming back
